name: Wave Offering
overview: The wave offering, as detailed in Exodus 29:22-27, was a sacred ritual involving specific portions of the consecration ram, including the fat, right shoulder, and breast, which were placed in the hands of the priest and waved before the Lord. This act signified the dedication of these parts to God as a pleasing aroma, symbolizing the priest's consecration and the people's devotion. The wave offering was not only a ceremonial presentation but also became the priest's portion, to be sanctified and eaten in a holy place by the priest's family, underscoring the intimate relationship between God, the priesthood, and the worship community.
